utterances.text: All right. One moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Yes, Mr. Bourgon?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. There is one further issue since we have time that we believe we should raise with the Trial Chamber at this time, and this has to do with the scheduling order which has been rendered by the Trial Chamber concerning the end of the case and the end of the presentation of the Prosecution's case. Pursuant to the schedule which was issued by the Trial Chamber, we would have to file and submit our Rule 65 ter summaries by the 31st of March and the first defence would begin on the 1st of June. We have been having been doing lots of discussions, both with the Prosecution and amongst ourselves, and we believe that we would like a delay for the submission of the Rule 65 ter summaries because a lot of the work that we do in preparation for the Defence case is work that needs to be done before these summaries are filed. So we are not ready at this time to provide the Trial Chamber with a definite proposal, but we would like to know how you would like us to submit this, whether in oral arguments or whether in writing. But basically our position is that we would like simply to -- start the 1st of June is a very good date. We have already begun working on our respective Defences, and we can meet this calendar and it's very good for us. Just the filing of the 65 ter summaries could be delayed to one month before that date. That gives us the time to investigate and give much better summaries to the Prosecution and the Trial Chamber. So that's one issue we would like to raise, and also the timing of the expert reports is something we would like to address at some point also in relation to this. So it's not the timing with the dates for the beginning of the Defence, 1 June is very good for us, it's just the timing of when we have to file specific information, either to give it to the Prosecution or to file it officially before the Trial Chamber. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. I suggest that you also deal with this when you meet with the Prosecution today or tomorrow, and/or tomorrow, because the timeliness of the filing of the Rule 65 ter lists is important not only to yourself and to us but also to the Prosecution that have to do their homework as well on it. So please discuss it and let us know what the respective positions are.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. President we just thought it would be appropriate to let you know that this is something we are looking into with the Prosecution already and we will continue to do so. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. McCloskey?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes. As I thought and got reminded by Ms. Stewart, Alistair Graham is also out there. We have been speaking about him with the Borovcanin team. I'm not sure we need to call him, but they may want to cross-examine him. This is something we have been talking about, but we need to resolve that as well. And we also have recently found a witness -- a very, very short witness. And so we'll be providing a motion to add a very short witness on to our list for January and that will be coming very soon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. I saw you standing, Mr. Josse.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: It was related to the matter that Mr. Bourgon mentioned, but bearing in mind how Your Honour thought we should proceed, I wasn't going to say anything at this particular juncture. Clearly, the Defence collectively will revert to the Trial Chamber if no agreement can be reached with the Prosecution. Could I briefly also whilst I'm on my feet mention Alistair Graham only in this context. I recall that when he was last before the Chamber, I for one on behalf of our client said that I would want him to return. Could I make it absolutely clear that unless the -- really the Borovcanin team want him to return, we are not asking him to return simply for the two or three questions that we might otherwise want to put to him. I hope I've made that clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you so much, Mr. Josse. Mr. Lazarevic, I saw you also standing.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, just to confirm that we had discussion with the Prosecution, but it was a while ago and then after that we simply forgot this topic. But I can assure the Trial Chamber that we will get in touch with the Prosecution and that you will have our position on this issue very soon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Do you need a chairman for the meetings, to prepare an agenda? Because it's growing by the minute.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, I believe that we'll manage to resolve this on our own.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. All right. Mr. McCloskey? So that brings today's sitting to an end. We will be at your disposal tomorrow. We will all be here. So if you encounter difficulties and you need to have a sitting at any time for any time tomorrow, we are at your disposal. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 10th day of December, 2007, at 9.00 a.m. 21 22 23 24 25
